headline: Governor HOCHUL 🏛️ SLAMS Cornell 🍆 RAPE Probe as TOTAL FAIL 🌪️
text:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul 🧑‍⚖️ just came out SWINGING 🥊 and declared the woman at the center of that Cornell 🏫 rape inquiry was straight up FAILED ❌ at every single turn 🛤️ by officials who dropped the ball 🏀 hard!! Jane Doe 📜 alleges she got DRUGGED 💊 and GANG RAPED by seven students at a frat house 🏠 back in 2024 and the initial probe just GHOSTED 👻 her completely with zero charges filed ⚖️. This whole mess got REOPENED after her civil lawsuit last month dropped the allegations into the national spotlight 🔦 like a bombshell 💣 and now Hochul is DEEPLY DISTURBED 😟 saying she lost all faith 🙏 in the local prosecutor to handle it right. She appointed Attorney General Letitia James 👩‍💼 to take over the reins 🏇 and lead a fresh investigation guided strictly by facts 📊 and the law ⚖️ while promising to interview every witness 🕵️ and pursue prosecutions if they stack up!! "This young woman endured something utterly unspeakable 😱 then got failed by people and institutions obligated to protect her" Hochul said at the news conference 📰 with pure outrage in her voice 📢. Some bystander was like bro she got RAILED 💦 by the system after already getting railed and that's just down bad 😤 for real.

Hochul straight up VOWED 🗣️ to close that disgusting loophole 🚪 that stops prosecutors from chasing rape charges when the victim voluntarily consumed drugs or alcohol 🍸 before the alleged gang bang 🥳!! Jane Doe is believed to have taken that stuff willingly on the night of the horror show 🎭 yet Hochul made it crystal clear "if someone is too intoxicated to consent it should not matter if they chose to use drugs or alcohol" and dropped the hammer with "voluntary intoxication is NOT a license for gang rape" 🚫🍆. James stood right beside her at the Friday presser 📸 pledging her office would run a process guided by facts 📋 and law 📜 while interviewing witnesses 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 left and right to see if charges are warranted after all. The local District Attorney Matthew Van Houten who ran the first investigation defended his crew saying they weren't given enough evidence to meet the legal threshold 📉 and much of the new info wasn't passed to his office in the first place 📦. He even dropped a statement supporting James now claiming it became clear the university never gave them the full picture 🖼️ and that has the whole campus looking cooked 🍳.

Cornell University itself insists it handed over evidence from its own internal investigation 🔎 including that wild Snapchat group chat 💬 where frat members casually discussed a "free" sexual encounter with Jane Doe on the night of the alleged assault 🏚️. Jane Doe filed her civil lawsuit against the Ivy League school in September and her lawyer Thomas Giuffra told CNN she's "not doing well" right now 🥀 while under siege on social media with creeps trying to dox her identity 🕵️‍♂️ and some fake court postings floating around to expose her further. Survivor advocates are screaming that current state law on sexual assault makes it nearly impossible to bring charges if the victim voluntarily drank or did drugs beforehand 🍹 which is exactly why this loophole bill was already crawling through the legislature before this week's public meltdown 🔥. Bronx District Attorney Darcel Clark pointed out "if a person goes out with friends and voluntarily consumes alcohol or drugs and becomes intoxicated so they're unable to say no and they're sexually assaulted that scenario is not covered by the current law" and everyone is nodding along like finally 📣.

Hochul said she will fully support the existing bill and it could zoom forward as early as the next legislative session that reconvenes in January ❄️ or she might even call lawmakers back early for a special session to ram it through 🏎️!! At the news conference she kept hammering how the young woman had already survived the unspeakable only to get betrayed by every institution meant to shield her 🛡️ and that the original handling raised seriously troubling questions about the entire process from start to finish 🌀. Students at Cornell are gathering in public hearings voicing their frustration and straight up anger over how this alleged frat house gang rape was swept under the rug 🧹 with some saying the university failed them too in protecting victims on campus 🏛️. The governor made it clear she lost all confidence in the local DA's office after learning new details that painted the investigation as sloppy at best and negligent at worst 🧨 which is why Letitia James is now stepping in with her full authority as the state's top legal officer 👑 to get real justice rolling at last ⚖️. One random observer whispered she got edged for months by bureaucracy before any real climax on accountability 😩 and that's just wild.

The appointment of James came right after Hochul publicly admitted she had zero faith left in the original team to oversee things fairly and that the accuser was never even interviewed properly by the prosecutors themselves during the first go around 🫥 which is straight up wild negligence in a case this heavy 🏋️. Van Houten pushed back claiming his office supported the new probe now and that the university held back key details like that group chat evidence which discussed the "free" encounter in graphic terms 🗣️ leaving his team without the full picture to even consider charges back then 📉. Advocates keep repeating that voluntary intoxication should never be a get out of jail free card for predators and Hochul is echoing that by promising to fix the law so no more victims get failed like Jane Doe was at every single turn 🔄. The civil suit has thrust everything into the spotlight forcing this reopening and now with James leading it witnesses will finally get grilled under the proper light 🔦 while the governor vows real change is coming whether in January or sooner via special session 🗓️. It's all so cooked that students are ashamed and protesting hard while the whole nation watches this Ivy League scandal unfold like a slow motion trainwreck 🚂💥 and Hochul is not letting it slide anymore period!!
